groups.title: Affective NNC foundation and attitude route
groups.proposal: Keep the two Canvas methods distinct: a compound affective nounstem expresses attitude through its matrix, while a flawed subject expresses attitude through the subject pronoun. Build both through the ordinary typed NNC owner and let the chosen grammatical structure, not a translation or example, select the route.
groups.writingJob: Represent compound-affective and flawed-subject Sources as distinct typed analyses, preserve the NNC subject and referent, and send the selected Source through ordinary NNC realization.
groups.readingJob: Show where the attitude is expressed, which referent it concerns, the compound embed and affective matrix when present, the later flawed-subject alternative, and why examples do not authorize either route.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended attitude and one of the two grammatical methods only when both are genuinely available for the typed Source. The application derives constituent order, matrix position, noun class, number, state, and realization.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the existing affective-NNC and NNC owners; do not add example, translation, matrix-position, class, boundary, or realization controls.

groups.title: The pīl and pōl affective matrices
groups.proposal: Treat pīl and pōl as lexical affective matrices whose compounds normally belong to the zero class regardless of the open typed embed: pīl contributes affectionate smallness and pōl contributes disparaging largeness. Preserve boundary phonology and keep a specially lexicalized tli-class Result as a typed lexical fact rather than a productive exception list.
groups.writingJob: Combine any compatible typed NNC embed with pīl or pōl, derive the zero-class Result automatically, apply regular boundary realization, and preserve a genuinely lexicalized special meaning and its tli-class reanalysis when supplied.
groups.readingJob: Show matrix identity and attitude, open embed admission, ordinary zero class, boundary changes, lexicalized tli-class contrast, number and state continuation, and examples as proof only.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended pīl or pōl attitude matrix. A lexicalized special meaning is supplied only when it is a real lexical fact; Result class and boundary form are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add stem whitelists, separate size and attitude controls, noun-class controls, example templates, or manual sound-change controls.

groups.title: The tzin matrix: class, meaning, and vocative use
groups.proposal: Use tzin as the typed affective matrix for special regard, honor, compassion, affection, cherished smallness, or mass delimitation. Derive zero class from a zero-class embed and tli class from every other compatible embed; preserve typed irregular variants, demonstrative formation, and the full-versus-abbreviated vocative contrast without turning them into example routes.
groups.writingJob: Build tzin compounds from open typed embeds, derive Result class from the embed class, preserve any genuine lexical boundary exception or demonstrative Source, and form full tzin or abbreviated tz vocatives through the vocative owner.
groups.readingJob: Show the selected tzin meaning, embed class, derived Result class, irregular or variant Source evidence, demonstrative and mass readings, vocative formality, the special il vocative facts, and examples as non-authorizing evidence.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses among genuinely intended tzin meanings when context does not settle them and chooses full versus abbreviated vocative when both are licensed. Class, boundaries, demonstrative structure, vocative particle, and formality consequences are automatic; lexical exceptions are typed facts.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse compound, noun-class, demonstrative, and vocative owners; do not add example, class, boundary, particle, or automatic-formality controls.

groups.title: The tōn matrix and class exceptions
groups.proposal: Use tōn for smallness without tzin's admiration or affection, derive zero class from a zero embed and tli otherwise, and keep the exceptional zero-class and boundary cases as typed lexical facts.
groups.writingJob: Build open tōn compounds, derive ordinary class from the embed, preserve recursive use, and apply only supplied lexical class or boundary exceptions.
groups.readingJob: Show neutral-smallness meaning, embed and Result classes, recursive embedding, exceptional class or boundary evidence, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses tōn when that meaning is intended and supplies a genuine lexical exception only when needed; class and realization are otherwise automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add animal lists, example templates, class controls, or manual boundary controls.

groups.title: The zol matrix, recursion, and denominal continuation
groups.proposal: Use zol as the nonanimate-only affective matrix for an old or worn-out entity, always derive a tli-class compound, allow its compound Results to recurse freely as embeds, and preserve its ordinary denominal VNC continuations separately from the restricted tzin and pōl continuations.
groups.writingJob: Build open nonanimate zol compounds, derive tli class, recapture owner-issued zol compounds recursively, and continue the completed zol Source through the licensed inchoative or causative denominal owners.
groups.readingJob: Show nonanimate restriction, worn-out meaning, tli class, recursion, inner and outer boundaries, denominal continuations, later restrictions on other matrices, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses zol and a licensed later continuation when intended. Animacy, class, recursive hierarchy, and derived VNC shape are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add object lists, depth controls, example routes, class controls, or manually assembled denominal stems.

groups.title: Affective affinity and absolutive plural number
groups.proposal: For a plural-subject compound affective NNC, reduplicate the affective matrix with the Canvas short-vowel affinity prefix and derive sounded t-in or silent zero-zero from the corresponding singular num1 behavior. Keep optional or obligatory double affinity on the embed as typed Source analysis.
groups.writingJob: Apply matrix affinity for plural subjects, preserve vowel quantity and boundaries, derive the absolutive plural dyad from singular num1, and add embed affinity only where typed analysis licenses or requires it.
groups.readingJob: Show plural subject, matrix reduplication, short-vowel contrast with Lesson 31, sounded or silent number dyad, demonstrative and supplementation readings, optional or obligatory double affinity, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The application applies matrix affinity and number automatically. The user chooses embed affinity only where typed analysis leaves a genuine optional alternative; obligatory double affinity is automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add vowel-length, number-dyad, example, or obligatory-scope controls.

groups.title: Possessive affinity number alternatives
groups.proposal: Form possessive plural affective NNCs from the same affinity-shaped compound and license hu-ān or silent zero-zero as the possessive number dyad, preserving the documented usage disagreement as real variation rather than a matrix whitelist.
groups.writingJob: Preserve possessor and plural subject, apply matrix affinity automatically, and realize the selected licensed hu-ān or silent possessive number dyad.
groups.readingJob: Show possessor, plural subject, affinity shape, both number dyads, frequency tendency, documentary disagreement, matrix independence, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses hu-ān versus silent number only where both are licensed; the application derives all other shape and agreement facts.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not turn a grammarian's example inventory into a pīl or pōl restriction.

groups.title: The pil lexeme and child formations
groups.proposal: Keep the simple nounstem pil 'appendage' distinct from the affective pīl matrix, preserve its child and noble lexical readings, and build the child possessive plural, unique outer tzin formation, distributive possessor, affinity plural, and gender-specific compounds from typed structure.
groups.writingJob: Carry the selected pil lexeme reading, possession, number, affinity, gender embed, and the unique owner-issued pil-hu-ān plus tzi-tzin hierarchy through canonical NNC composition.
groups.readingJob: Show appendage history, child versus conē contrast, child or noble ambiguity, possession, unique relic structure, distributive possessor, gender specificity, affinity, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses child versus noble only where the NNC is genuinely ambiguous and chooses gender specification when intended. Possession, number, hierarchy, and required affinity are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not collapse pil and pīl, infer meaning from English, or add example, hierarchy, boundary, or automatic-affinity controls.

groups.title: Affective child matrices
groups.proposal: Build the child reading of pil with tzin, tōn, pīl, or pōl matrices and apply affinity to both embed and matrix automatically for plural absolutive subjects, while preserving possessive and vocative continuations.
groups.writingJob: Select the intended affective child matrix, derive class and singular or plural affinity, preserve possession, and continue through the full or abbreviated vocative construction.
groups.readingJob: Show child meaning, matrix attitude, singular and plural forms, double affinity, possession, vocative meaning shifts, beloved-child contrast, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the affective matrix and a genuinely available vocative form; class, double affinity, possession, and surface realization are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add child-stem templates, class controls, separate double-affinity controls, or translation-derived vocative routes.

groups.title: pil noble and honorific formations
groups.proposal: Preserve pil's noble reading in absolutive NNCs, yō-matrix possession in possessive NNCs, and the unique singular honorific pil-tzin-tzin vocative without misreading the repeated tzin sequence as affinity.
groups.writingJob: Build simple or gender-specific noble NNCs, preserve child-versus-noble ambiguity, derive pil-lō possession through yō, and build the nested singular honorific vocative as typed recursion rather than reduplication.
groups.readingJob: Show noble meaning, gender custom, ambiguity, yō possession, nobility or childishness contrast, singular honorific recursion, absence of affinity, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses noble versus child only where genuinely ambiguous and chooses the intended singular vocative; yō possession, recursion, and non-affinity diagnosis are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not infer meaning from gender or surface repetition and do not add manual yō, bracketing, or reduplication controls.

groups.title: Nonanimate affinity and supplement agreement
groups.proposal: Allow the Canvas-marked nonanimate compound affective NNC to take plural t-in under affinity, while preserving its common-number behavior as a supplement and the genuine affinity-versus-distributive meaning ambiguity of nonanimate matrix reduplication.
groups.writingJob: Build the licensed nonanimate plural affective NNC, retain the separate common-number supplement head relation, and carry affinity or distributive-varietal scope as typed contextual analysis.
groups.readingJob: Show nonanimate status, plural surface number, common-number supplement agreement, head and supplement references, affinity or distributive meaning, contextual evidence, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses affinity versus distributive-varietal only when context truly leaves both readings open. Number realization and supplement agreement are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not regularize the number discrepancy, infer meaning from reduplicative shape alone, or create example-stem gates.

groups.title: Flawed-subject NNCs
groups.proposal: Use a typed flawed-subject analysis to replace sounded ti, tli, or in num1 with the irregular silent variant only in singular or common-number absolutive NNCs whose lexical meaning and context license disparagement, while keeping defect-entity ambiguity, alternative zero-class stems, affective consequences, and unrelated silent-num1 procedures distinct.
groups.writingJob: Apply the silent num1 variant under the exact state, number, and lexical conditions; preserve stem shape, noun class, defect versus entity reading, affective-matrix consequences, and plural restoration through the ordinary NNC owner.
groups.readingJob: Show sounded and flawed contrast, attitude, defect or entity meaning, state and number limits, Source shape and pronominal case, alternative stem class, forced flawing under tzin or tōn, unrelated silent-num1 procedures, chicken lexicalization, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses a flawed-subject reading only where the typed lexeme and context genuinely permit both neutral and disparaging forms, and chooses defect versus entity only for real lexical ambiguity. All shape and inflectional consequences are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not use the listed defect stems as a productive route whitelist; exact identities may remain only for genuinely lexical or defective facts. Do not merge flawed subjects with adverbial or personal-name silent num1.
